acceptance_criteria.criterion: ProjectData interface in project.types.ts includes LastActivity?: string as an optional field.
updateLastActivity() sets LastActivity on the project JSON file and does NOT modify DateModified.
updateLastActivity() short-circuits without writing to disk when the new value equals the existing LastActivity value.
updateLastActivity() silently returns (no error thrown) when called with a project ID that does not exist.
All existing project manager tests continue to pass.
New unit tests in project.manager.test.ts verify all four behaviours above.
All TypeScript imports use .js extensions per the Node16 ESM requirement.

summary: Added LastActivity?: string as an optional field to the ProjectData interface in project.types.ts with a JSDoc comment explaining its semantics.

Implemented updateLastActivity(id, value) on ProjectManager: loads the project, returns silently if not found, short-circuits without a disk write when the new value equals the existing LastActivity, otherwise sets LastActivity and persists via saveProject() without touching DateModified.

Added four new unit tests in project.manager.test.ts covering: (1) sets LastActivity correctly, (2) does not modify DateModified, (3) short-circuits (file mtime unchanged) when value is already equal, (4) silently returns for a nonexistent project ID.
All 756 tests pass. TypeScript compiles cleanly with --noEmit.

comments.note: project.manager.ts: The private now() helper (line ~80) is a one-liner that could be inlined, but keeping it as a named method is perfectly fine for testability and readability — no action needed.

project.types.ts: SchemaVersion is a bare number with no JSDoc and no schema migration strategy documented anywhere in the types file. As new optional fields (e.g. LastActivity) are added without bumping SCHEMA_VERSION in project.manager.ts, existing JSON files silently read as valid — this is correct but worth documenting explicitly so future contributors don't inadvertently bump the version for non-breaking additions.

project.manager.ts: updateLastActivity does not return the updated ProjectData (unlike every other mutating method). This is intentional per the spec (void return), but if the method is later used by the API layer it may require a signature change. A brief JSDoc note on the void return would aid future readers.

comments.note: project.manager.ts updateLastActivity(): The method has no JSDoc on its void return. Minor — but noting per the Developer's own improvement comment. No blocking issue.

Mtime-based short-circuit test (line 639): Test is deterministic on APFS (macOS). On CI environments using FAT/exFAT/HFS+ (2-second mtime granularity), the test could theoretically be flaky. Current CI environment is APFS — no action needed, but worth flagging for future Docker-based CI images if they use tmpfs or FAT-backed volumes.
No observations of code quality issues beyond the low-priority items already flagged by the Developer. Implementation is clean, minimal, and well-tested.

New optional fields like LastActivity are backward-compatible and correctly do not bump the version, but this convention is nowhere documented. Add a JSDoc comment to SchemaVersion explaining: (1) what the version tracks, (2) that adding optional fields is non-breaking and does NOT require a bump, and (3) what kinds of changes DO require a bump.

notes: All seven acceptance criteria are met and verified by the test suite (756/756 pass). The implementation is minimal and stateless — no caches, no side-effects beyond the single JSON file write. The short-circuit uses a strict equality check on the string value, which is correct for ISO 8601 timestamps. QA should confirm the mtime-based short-circuit test is deterministic on CI (it relies on filesystem mtime resolution; on most systems this is 1 ms or better, but on FAT/HFS+ volumes with 2-second mtime granularity the test could be flaky).
